On an explicit request for a council of named models (.claude/skills/model-council/SKILL.md:3), model-council runs one common brief through user-selected members in isolation, parallel where useful; the brief asks each member for its strongest answer, not a hedge toward what a panel might favour, because differences between members are the evidence, and no member sees another's answer (.claude/skills/model-council/SKILL.md:8-9, 18-24). For a built artifact such as a design sketch it adds pick-and-graft (.claude/skills/model-council/SKILL.md:31-32): each member writes only to its own location, and a judge and then the coordinator score every candidate on stated criteria and pick a base (.claude/skills/model-council/references/pick-and-graft.md:6-23). Without a council, codebase-design sketches materially different designs, optionally through bounded independent workers, and never forces a multi-agent exercise (.claude/skills/codebase-design/DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md:8-10). Delegation stays matched to the task (U-07) and the exercise is not an absolute rule (S-08).
